summary: Both round-1 mediums are fixed. M1: a background change no longer dims or goes black. In src/ui/story/backdrop.js the old layers are now removed only after the new layer has faded in. That means its own opacity transitionend, or FADE_FALLBACK_MS (670 ms) counted from when 'on' is added, and its picture has decoded. Removal goes through layersToDrop(), so only layers beneath the topmost fully-in layer are removed. I recorded every rAF frame (layer count and computed opacity) and a CDP screencast through 10 background changes. These covered ch6.epi, ch2.epi and ch7.epi at 844x390, and ch3.epi, ch7.epi and ch2.epi at 1280x720, with CPU throttling at 1x, 4x and 6x (Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate). Three runs added 250 ms main-thread stalls right after each picture decoded. In all 10 runs, 0 of about 9,400 frames had no layer at full opacity. In the stall runs, the old layer stayed at 1.00 until the new one read 0.88 to 0.95, and the next frame showed the new one alone at 1.00. No screencast frame dipped in luminance in the background corners. The only near-black frames were the scene's own exit after its last line, which is expected. The branch's own e2e check (e2e/story.mjs at 844x390, 0 of 330 bare frames) and tests/story (136 tests) pass. M2: festival-drum now shows one big taiko drum on a wooden stand on a stage, centred, in a lantern-lined square under fireworks. There is no blank sheet or sign and no fake writing. It matches festival-street and the rest of the set in palette, paving and lantern style. With focus 54% 40% the whole drum sits above the text box at 844x390, 1280x720 and 932x430. At 390x844 it fills the middle, slightly left of centre and fully in frame. The narration lines that name the great drum (ch7.mid line 1, ch7.epi line 1) show it unobstructed. The WebP has no EXIF or XMP. The new tools/story-bg prompts are SFW scenery with no people in the game's own style words, and they name no game, anime or artist. The regression pass found nothing new above low. L1 to L5 stand. L6 is fixed: STORY_SPEC now names the Halloween scenes. Two new low notes are about the drum picture's staging.

findings.title: Staging: a centred portrait hides the drum on lines that name it, and in the archive thumbs
findings.detail: In ch7.epi, Hikari's centred stand covers the drum on 'Time to sing again, old drum. First light.' and on the narration 'The great drum sounds again…', at 844x390, 1280x720 and 390x844. The Episode 2 and 3 archive cards (ch7.mid, ch7.epi) put their portrait over the middle of the thumb, so the drum barely shows there. The drum is fully visible on each scene's first line, so the place reads. Moving Hikari to a side slot for those two lines would show the drum while it is named. This is scene and archive staging, not the picture.
